# Settings portability: review round 2

Reviewer: Fable 5.1, review only (owner approved 5.1 because 5.2 is unavailable). Diff `git diff 3f5eb31 9731cee -- app build.gradle.kts settings_portability settings_rescue`, HEAD 9731cee. Nothing was built or run. The only file written is this one. About 25 minutes.

Read in full: the diff; both new test files; the new `RecoveryComponents.kt` and `SettingsStartup.kt` in settings_portability; app `ProcessStores`, `SettingsStartup`, `RecoveryComponents`, `RecoveryActivity`, `FarhanApplication`, `PrivateSettingsFiles`, `SettingsBackupActivity` around the dialog; `ImportCoordinator` and `ImportJournal` for the startup contract; rescue `RescueActivity` layout helpers, `CaptureEngine` constructor, `AdbBridgeService.withConnection`, cancel path, manifest and strings; root and module Gradle files; round-1 review, argument and fixes reports; the ledger.

Evidence I checked myself, not taken from the reports:

- JUnit XML under `captures/settings/build-attempt2`: portability 59 tests, rescue 56 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped. `RecoveryComponentsTest` (7) and `SettingsStartupTest` (7) are in the portability run, so the 14 new tests executed under the real Android Gradle invocation.
- Merged app manifest in `captures/settings/build-attempt2/evidence/app-manifest.xml:177-193`: `LegacySenderService`, `JobSenderService` and `AcraContentProvider` all declare `android:process=":acra"`. The round-1 hardening item is now a confirmed path, not a memory.
- ACRA 5.12.0 `ACRA.kt` (fetched, tag acra-5.12.0): `object ACRA`, `@JvmStatic fun isACRASenderServiceProcess(): Boolean`, public, matches `/proc/self/cmdline` against `":acra"`. The Kotlin call in `FarhanApplication.kt:34` resolves. Not compiled here.
- Merged rescue manifest before the fix listed `WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`, `READ_PHONE_STATE`, `READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`. Those three are the manifest merger's implied permissions for a library AAR with no `targetSdkVersion`, not permissions from `:settings_android`. Removing them is correct.
- No code outside `ProcessStores` opens `shared_pref`, `farhan_data_store` or `farhan_db` (grep over app, core, core_ui, notification_filter, settings_android). The gate covers every consumer; `AppModule.kt:45,53,85` are the only providers.
- Build log `boat-build-20261118T075152Z.log`: the root build configured `:settings_portability`, ran its tests, compiled `:settings_rescue`, and failed only at `:app:compileDebugKotlin:91` on the `Button` receiver. That failure is the line fixed in this diff.

## Round-1 findings

- **S1 resolved.** `RecoveryComponentProtocol.heal()` (`settings_portability/.../RecoveryComponents.kt:71-79`) filters the snapshot by `normalComponents()` names before any `set`. `healingSkipsRemovedAndLeavesNewComponentsAlone` pins it, and the Rig's `set` throws for a removed name, so dropping the filter goes red. New components are untouched, and `blockExtendsSnapshotForNewComponents` pins the snapshot extension before the new component's disable.
- **S2 resolved as a code and test finding.** The protocol, gate and coordinator are real production classes; the Android adapter has no branching beyond PackageManager calls and a `toInt` map. I ran the round-1 mutations in my head against the tests: `snapshot.write` after the disable loop fails `snapshotPrecedesDisablesAndRepeatedBlockDoesNothing` on the literal event list; `gate.open()` before `heal()` fails `healRunsWithEveryStoreStillDenied` because heal asserts denial; dropping `snapshot.clear()` fails the `assertNull(saved)` checks; dropping `gate.close()` fails the test that opens the gate first; dropping the catch-path `block()` fails `healFailureKeepsGateClosedAndBlocksComponents`; dropping the `components.get(name) != expected` guard fails on the event list (Hidden and UserDisabled would be written). The crash test walks all eight durable boundaries with a fresh platform built only from durable maps. The instrumented `AndroidImportJournal` test is still unrun; that is the open gate below, as agreed in round 1.
- **S3 resolved.** Intro, export body, SOURCE_CHANGED and after-save text say turn off the old Farhan's notification access before export, keep it closed, and check both permissions afterwards if the old app is kept. Force-stop "may" turn off accessibility; no version range, no rebind claim. The shortcut opens `ACTION_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_SETTINGS` with a plain Settings fallback. The owner can now act on the error. The Pixel 9a device check remains evidence, not a bar item.
- **S4 resolved.** The root build configured `:settings_portability` with the `jetbrainsKotlinJvm apply false` line present (attempt 1 and attempt 2 logs). Whether it would also have configured without the line is unknown and does not matter: the line is the conventional form and the build is observed to configure.

## New findings

None at blocker or should. I looked for an in-scope failure in the new code and did not find one. What follows is a verification gate, not a defect.

The code I read reaches durability 9 only once four facts that no JVM test can establish have been observed. Two of the diff's lines (`FarhanApplication.kt:34`, `SettingsBackupActivity.kt:91`) are uncompiled, the production journal has never round-tripped a record on Android, and the Android component adapter has never executed. The adapter maps two platform behaviours nobody has watched: `ComponentInfo.enabled` for manifest-disabled components under `GET_DISABLED_COMPONENTS`, and `setComponentEnabledSetting(..., DEFAULT, DONT_KILL_APP)` restoring WorkManager's explicitly ENABLED proxies. The protocol is correct on paper; the paper has to meet the phone once.

Gates, in the order that gives the most information per minute:

1. Full assemble of 9731cee for both APKs. Resolves the two uncompiled corrections.
2. Instrumented `AndroidImportJournal` test: every phase round-trips, including `previous` with raw values of the "wrong" type.
3. On the Pixel 9a (debuggable build): capture `dumpsys package ly.com.tahaben.farhan` component states; write garbage into `no_backup/settings_import_v1` with `run-as`; launch; confirm every normal component is disabled and the recovery icon appears; delete the garbage; launch; confirm `dumpsys` states equal the capture byte for byte and the recovery icon is gone. This is the one run that proves the adapter.
4. Stage a real export, kill, relaunch, see Applied, acknowledge; then roll back once by making a store fail if that is cheap, otherwise accept the JVM rollback tests.

Gates 1 to 4 passing moves durability to 9 and the verdict to APPROVE with no further code round. The S3 pidof and accessibility check and the real helper pair, export, import run are the pilot's owner evidence (`owner-ok`), not conditions for the bar.

## Scores

SCORE[durability]: 8/10 (every round-1 defect is fixed and pinned by tests that executed; held at 8 until gates 1 to 4 above have run, as round 1 agreed; bar 9)
SCORE[error-paths]: 8/10 (fail-closed paths are pinned on the production classes; SOURCE_CHANGED advice is actionable; stashed nits only; bar 6)
SCORE[security]: 8/10 (no in-model exposure; three implied permissions removed from the helper; the `:acra` process no longer touches the journal; bar 6)
SCORE[architecture]: 8/10 (the port extraction is the right shape and the adapter stayed thin; root build configures; bar 6)
SCORE[legibility]: 8/10 (claims cite the test that proves them; two comment nits below; bar 6)
VERDICT: CHANGES (durability 8 against a bar of 9. No new source change is needed for the bar. The change is: run gates 1 to 4 and record the results. Pass means APPROVE without another code round.)

## For the two dialogue tasks

Exchange A, the one that matters: is gate 3 the minimum device evidence, or do the JVM protocol tests plus a thin adapter suffice for 9? My position: gate 3 is the minimum. The adapter is thin but it is where the only unobserved platform facts live, and a wrong `ComponentInfo.enabled` reading would disable a manifest-disabled component or skip an enabled one on every blocked start. One run, ten minutes, settles it. I will not move to 9 on reasoning alone.

Exchange B, the one I want the parent to push back on: `SettingsStoreGate.open()` and `close()` are public, and `ProcessStores.gate` is internal to the app module, so any app code can open the gate before heal. Nothing does today. Making both `internal` to settings_portability costs two keywords, needs no test, and removes the class at layer 1 of the enforcement ladder. The parent may call it hardening because no caller exists. I would accept that, but the checkpoint's question 4 should record which layer holds this class and why.

COMMENT-FIXUPS: none (review brief restricts writes to this file)

NIT-STASH:
- settings_portability/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/settings_portability/SettingsStartup.kt:8-9 `open()` and `close()` can be `internal`; only `SettingsStartupCoordinator` needs them. One central change, no test needed.
- settings_rescue/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:9 The comment attributes every removed permission to `:settings_android`, `notification_filter_data` and `:core`. The three new ones are merger-implied permissions from a library AAR without `targetSdkVersion`. Split the comment or name the source once the manifest-merger report shows which AAR.
- app/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan/FarhanApplication.kt:32-33 CLAIM(recovery-single-process) cites a research report. Cite the observed source instead: `captures/settings/build-attempt2/evidence/app-manifest.xml:177-193` and the ACRA 5.12.0 `ACRA.kt` line.
- settings_portability/src/test/java/ly/com/tahaben/settings_portability/RecoveryComponentsTest.kt:146 `validate()` has a value case but no name case. A snapshot holding the marker name or a name without a dot is never rejected by a test. Add one line to `snapshotAndToggleFailuresRemainRecoverable`.

HARDENING-STASH:
- settings_rescue/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan_rescue/ui/RescueActivity.kt:515 On API 30 and later, `ACTION_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_DETAIL_SETTINGS` with `EXTRA_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_COMPONENT_NAME` opens the old Farhan's listener row directly. Polish only; the generic page works.
- settings_rescue/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan_rescue/capture/CaptureEngine.kt:92 (pre-existing) `throwIfCancelled` is tested in `CaptureEngineTest` but no production caller passes it; cancel works by killing the bridge process (CLAIM(real-cancel)). Either wire a volatile flag from the cancel message or drop the parameter and its test case, so the suite does not prove a capability the product never uses.

# Settings portability review fixes

Status: source batch complete, **not compiled or run**. No builds, test jobs, Boat, emulators, commits or infrastructure actions. Parent owns verification. `git diff --check` passed for owned paths. Existing evidence of 45 core and 56 helper JVM tests predates these changes; the 14 new tests remain unrun.

## S1 and S2

`settings_portability/RecoveryComponents.kt` contains the production `RecoveryComponentProtocol`, `ComponentStates` and durable `ComponentStateSnapshot` ports. Android `RecoveryComponents` now only adapts PackageManager enumeration/raw overrides and the existing PrivateSettingsFile. RecoveryActivity's existing calls reach the same extracted production protocol.

Block enables the recovery marker first, extends and durably writes the full raw override snapshot before disabling any normal component, and returns true only when it changed a normal component. Repeated block does not rewrite an unchanged snapshot or marker. Heal enumerates current components, skips saved names removed by an update, restores exact overrides for existing saved names, leaves unrecorded new components untouched, clears the snapshot and disables the marker last. Invalid or unreadable snapshots still throw and fail closed. Marker-off healing performs no writes or snapshot reads.

`settings_portability/SettingsStartup.kt` contains the default-deny `SettingsStoreGate` and production `SettingsStartupCoordinator`. Actual ProcessStores public getters use gate.access with the same three lazy instances that private importer ports access directly. Startup closes the gate, runs the real importer, heals components, then opens the gate. Blocking results or Exceptions leave the gate closed and invoke block; process kill is requested only if block returns changed. Errors propagate. Android SettingsStartup retains Thread/join and Process.killProcess only; an Error in the worker is rethrown after join. No journal abstraction or ACRA process API was added. The existing SettingsBackupActivity lifecycle change was untouched.

Fourteen new focused JVM tests exercise these actual production classes. They pin literal mutation order, exact raw overrides including WorkManager-style ENABLED and disabled variants, repeated block, new and removed components, corrupt/write/toggle failures, eight crash positions across block/heal, lazy factory denial, one-instance reuse, no-journal startup through the real ImportCoordinator, gate denial during heal and block, heal failure, kill-only-if-changed, process-death Error propagation and zero-write healthy startup. Crash replay creates a fresh fake platform from only its durable component/snapshot maps and then a fresh protocol. The heal-before-open test would fail if gate.open moved before heal. The snapshot-order test would fail if snapshot.write moved after normal disables; the clear assertion would fail if snapshot.clear were dropped. No mutation runs were performed in this batch.

## S3 and S4

Helper introduction, export preparation, SOURCE_CHANGED and after-save text now instruct turning off OLD Farhan notification access before export, keeping it closed until save, and checking/re-enabling notification/accessibility access if retaining the old app. Wording says force-stop **may** turn off accessibility services. It makes no categorical Android-version or listener-restart claim. A notification-access Settings shortcut was added with a generic Settings fallback. No permissions are changed automatically and no ADB command was added. The existing SIZE_ONLY note is preserved.

The root plugins block now declares `alias(libs.plugins.jetbrainsKotlinJvm) apply false`. No observed Gradle failure is claimed; the full build/configuration gate remains to be run.

## Check-in

Parent accepted reconstructing fake platform state only from durable maps, keeping literal event-order expectations, using the real no-journal ImportCoordinator with the same lazy gate seam, and asserting denial in both heal and block. No design ambiguity remained. Android journal instrumentation remains a separate unrun runtime gate. Android compilation, device behavior, merged providers/processes, startup timing and the physical source-to-file-to-import path remain unverified.

## Parent build attempt

The full root build configured successfully and compiled the shared Android settings library. It then failed at `:settings_rescue:compileDebugKotlin`: two trailing progress lambdas bound to the final cancellation callback instead of `reportProgress`. Both bridge call sites now name `reportProgress`. This correction is not yet compiled. The bounded runner requested a non-forced sandbox stop immediately after the failed build. The 14 new recovery tests are queued locally; no new passing test count is claimed. Build log: `captures/settings/boat-build-20261118T073733Z.log`.

## Parent incremental verification

The actual Android Gradle tasks passed 59 portability and 56 rescue unit tests, with zero failures/errors/skips. This includes all 14 new recovery tests. XML is copied under `captures/settings/build-attempt2`. The helper compiled, but `:app:compileDebugKotlin` found an Activity context shadowed by a Button receiver in the unsupported-key dialog. That builder now names `this@SettingsBackupActivity`; this final correction remains uncompiled. No current APK is certified by this failed build. The archive contains an older app APK, which must not be delivered as the settings build.

Merged-manifest inspection confirmed ACRA sender services and its provider use `:acra`, supplying the evidence absent in round 1. FarhanApplication now returns before settings startup and Hilt in that process, using the actual public method in [pinned ACRA 5.12.0 source](https://github.com/ACRA/acra/blob/acra-5.12.0/acra-core/src/main/java/org/acra/ACRA.kt#L179). No journal lock or new process abstraction was added. The helper manifest had three unused transitive phone/storage permissions; its own manifest now removes them. Both manifest/source corrections await a fresh Android build. Runtime journal tests, pairing and physical export/import remain unrun.

package ly.com.tahaben.farhan.settings

import android.content.Context
import android.content.pm.PackageManager

import ly.com.tahaben.settings_portability.ComponentStateSnapshot

import ly.com.tahaben.settings_portability.RecoveryControl
import java.io.File

/** Android ports only; block/heal ordering lives in the JVM-tested production protocol. */
internal class RecoveryComponents(context: Context) : RecoveryControl {
    private val manager = context.packageManager
    private val marker = ComponentName(context, RecoveryActivity::class.java).className
    private val file = PrivateSettingsFile(File(context.noBackupFilesDir, "component_states_v1"))
    private val protocol = RecoveryComponentProtocol(marker, object : ComponentStates {
        @Suppress("DEPRECATION")
        override fun list(): List<RecoveryComponent> {
            val info = manager.getPackageInfo(context.packageName, PackageManager.GET_ACTIVITIES or
                PackageManager.GET_SERVICES or PackageManager.GET_RECEIVERS or PackageManager.GET_PROVIDERS or PackageManager.GET_DISABLED_COMPONENTS)
            return (info.activities.orEmpty().toList() + info.services.orEmpty().toList() +
                info.receivers.orEmpty().toList() + info.providers.orEmpty().toList())
                .map { RecoveryComponent(it.name, it.enabled) }
        }
        override fun get(name: String) = manager.getComponentEnabledSetting(ComponentName(context.packageName, name))
        override fun set(name: String, state: Int) = manager.setComponentEnabledSetting(
            ComponentName(context.packageName, name), state, PackageManager.DONT_KILL_APP)
    }, object : ComponentStateSnapshot {
        override fun read() = file.read()?.mapValues { it.value.toInt() }
        override fun write(states: Map<String, Int>) = file.write(states.mapValues { it.value.toString() })
        override fun clear() = file.clear()
    })
    override fun block() = protocol.block()
    override fun heal() = protocol.heal()
}

# Writing copy

Load `unslop` and `plain-writing` first, then apply these six rules.

1. **No eyebrow lines.** Omit the small label or kicker above a heading or
   title unless the request asks for one.
2. **Question every piece of text.** Name the question it answers and whether
   anyone is really asking it. People usually are not. Cut it if not.
3. **Keep jargon out of explainers.** One word per idea, defined once. Reuse
   that word; do not cycle synonyms.
4. **One named audience.** Know who reads it before you write, and write for
   that person.
5. **No compliance narration.** Do not explain how an action follows a rule
   or why it does not break one, unless the reader asked or the action really
   sits on the rule's boundary; then state the decision in one clause and stop.
   Never explain a distinction the reader set up or plainly knows. After a
   correction, report what changed; do not reassure in later messages. The
   test: what would the reader misread without this sentence? If nothing, cut
   it.
6. **Three passes before sending.** Reread the whole draft three times, each
   pass with one question: is every claim correct; does every sentence answer
   something the reader is asking; is any sentence about the writer rather
   than the reader's subject (self-justification, reassurance, credit, effort).
   Take the most care with that last kind: it is the easiest to miss in your

# Unslop

Edit text to remove AI patterns and add human voice.

## Process

1. Scan for the patterns below.
2. Rewrite. Preserve meaning, match intended tone.
3. Add soul (see next section).
4. Self-audit: "What makes this obviously AI generated?" Fix remaining tells.

## Adding soul

Removing patterns is half the job. Sterile, voiceless writing is just as obvious.

- **Have opinions.** React to facts instead of neutrally listing pros and cons.
- **Vary rhythm.** Short sentences. Then longer ones that take their time. Mix it up.
- **Acknowledge complexity.** "Impressive but also kind of unsettling" beats "impressive."
- **Use "I" when it fits.** First person isn't unprofessional.
- **Let some mess in.** Perfect structure looks machine-made.
- **Be specific.** Not "this is concerning" but "there's something unsettling about agents churning away at 3am."

## Patterns to detect and fix

### Content

1. **Puffery.** "pivotal moment", "testament to", "evolving landscape", "setting the stage for", "indelible mark", "deeply rooted". Cut puffery, state what happened.
2. **Name-dropping.** Listing media outlets without context. Pick one, say what was said.
3. **Superficial -ing phrases.** "highlighting...", "ensuring...", "reflecting...", "showcasing...", "fostering...". Delete or expand with real sources.
4. **Promotional language.** "nestled", "vibrant", "breathtaking", "groundbreaking", "renowned", "stunning", "must-visit". Use neutral descriptions.
5. **Vague attributions.** "Experts believe", "Industry reports suggest", "Some critics argue". Name the source or delete.
6. **Formulaic challenges.** "Despite challenges... continues to thrive." Replace with specific facts.

### Language

7. **AI vocabulary.** Additionally, crucial, delve, enduring, enhance, fostering, garner, interplay, intricate, landscape (abstract), pivotal, showcase, tapestry (abstract), testament, underscore, vibrant. Replace with plain words.
8. **Fancy ways to say "is".** "serves as", "stands as", "boasts", "features". Just say "is" or "has".
9. **"Not just X, but Y."** State the point directly instead.
10. **Unsupported contrasts.** Do not rebut a diagnosis the reader has not made. Remove phrases such as "not X," "rather than X," "as opposed to X," or "this isn't X" unless X was explicitly claimed earlier. Even when a comparison is useful or requested, state the positive evidence and evaluation path instead of negating X. Ask: "Who claimed X?" If the answer is nobody, state the supported fact directly.
11. **Rule of three.** Forcing ideas into groups of three. Use the natural number.
12. **Synonym cycling.** Protagonist, main character, central figure, hero all in one paragraph. Pick one, repeat it.
13. **False ranges.** "from X to Y" where X and Y aren't on a meaningful scale. List topics directly.

### Style

13. **Em dash overuse.** Avoid em dashes entirely. Use periods or commas only (no parentheses, no en dashes, no hyphen-as-dash substitutes). Em dashes are an AI tell, and reaching for parentheses instead just trades one tell for another. If a thought needs separation, end the sentence or use a comma.
14. **Colon overuse.** Colons are fine before a list or example. Not as mid-sentence connectors. "If you're coming from traditional automation: instead of registering event handlers, you describe conditions" adds nothing with the colon. Rewrite to let the point stand on its own without comparison framing. "Describing when the scheduler should fire works best as plain English." Same meaning, no crutch punctuation.
15. **Boldface overuse.** Don't bold every proper noun or acronym.
16. **Inline-header lists.** The tell is a bold label and colon that restates the line: "**Performance:** Performance improved...". Convert those to prose. A bold lead-in that ends in a period, names the item, and is followed by genuinely new detail ("**Schema in TypeScript.** Tables live in one file.") is fine, not a tell.
17. **Title case headings.** Use sentence case.
18. **Decorative emojis.** Remove from headings and bullets.
19. **Curly quotes.** Replace with straight quotes.

### Communication artifacts

20. **Chatbot phrases.** "I hope this helps!", "Let me know if...", "Of course!", "Certainly!", "Found the smoking gun!" Remove.
21. **Cutoff disclaimers.** "While specific details are limited..." Find sources or remove.
22. **Sycophantic tone.** "Great question! You're absolutely right!" Respond directly.

### Filler

23. **Filler phrases.** "In order to" becomes "To". "Due to the fact that" becomes "Because". "It is important to note that" gets deleted.
24. **Excessive hedging.** "could potentially possibly be argued that it might" becomes "may".
25. **Generic conclusions.** "The future looks bright." State specific plans or facts.

### Jargon

26. **Abstract metaphor nouns.** Substrate, wedge, vector, locus, vantage, nexus, primitive (as noun), harness (as metaphor), surface (as in "API surface"), bedrock, scaffolding (as metaphor), modality, paradigm, gold-plating, ratchet (as metaphor), evacuate (for moving code), endgame, north star, flywheel. These read as technical but usually have a plainer concrete word. "Substrate" becomes "base". "Wedge in" becomes "add". "Vector" becomes "way" or "method". "Gold-plating" becomes "more than the job needs". "Ratchet" becomes the mechanism's real name or "a limit that only tightens". "Evacuate" becomes "move out". "Endgame" becomes "the last phase". Pick the concrete word.

### Plain speech

27. **Say what it does, not how it feels.** "the database stays close at hand", "SQL you can read", "types that follow your schema" name a feeling. The fix names the mechanism or a number: "`.toSQL()` returns the exact string sent to the database", "a column rename fails the build". Ask what the sentence tells the reader to do or know, then write that. If you can't restate it as a concrete instruction, fact, or number, cut it. One more check: if the sentence could appear unchanged in another project's docs, it says nothing about this one. Cut it.
28. **Shorten or split dense sentences.** If the reader has to backtrack to parse a sentence, break it in two or drop clauses. One idea per sentence.
29. **Active voice.** Prefer it. Catch "is/are/was/were + past participle" and name the actor: "queries are validated" becomes "the compiler validates queries", "the file is parsed by the loader" becomes "the loader parses the file". Passive is fine only when the actor is unknown or genuinely doesn't matter.
30. **Cut adverbs, or use a stronger verb.** "runs quickly" becomes "is fast" or the number. "significantly improves" becomes the measured delta. An adverb propping up a weak verb means the verb is wrong.
31. **Prefer the plain word.** "utilize" becomes "use", "leverage" becomes "use", "facilitate" becomes "help", "numerous" becomes "many", "in the event that" becomes "if". The fancier synonym is rarely clearer.

# Plain writing

Write plain and direct. Apply from the first sentence, to your own replies and
summaries as much as to drafts you're handed.

## Three vices to cut

**1. Deep jargon.** An acronym or insider term used without defining it, or
several undefined terms stacked in one sentence. Define each term in a few plain
words on first use, or don't use it. Covers corporate shorthand, not just
technical terms.
- No: "We'll leverage the Q3 GTM motion to move the needle on NRR."
- Yes: "In the third quarter we'll aim the sales plan at getting current
  customers to spend more."
- Reuse the short form after one definition: "annual recurring revenue (ARR) —
  the subscription income we count on each year" then "ARR."

**2. Throat-clearing.** Preamble and narration about what the text is about to
do. Don't announce structure, editorialize your reasoning, or warm up. Cut "it's
worth being concrete," "before we get into it," "the honest truth is," "this is
the part that matters most."
- No: "Before the details, it's worth stepping back. The honest truth is
  onboarding is broken."
- Yes: "Onboarding is broken: four in ten new users quit before finishing setup."
- Cousin — claiming a virtue instead of showing it: "the honest answer," "to be
  fair," "frankly," "the real question." Delete the label, keep the sentence.

**3. Showing off.** Flourish that sounds clever instead of informing. No
rhetorical triads, aphorisms, italics for drama, cute headings, or punchline
sentences. Cut any sentence doing rhetorical work rather than carrying
information.
- No: "We shipped fast, we shipped hard, and we shipped it *beautiful*."
- Yes: "We shipped the redesign in six weeks."
- Also cut the stacked "not X; Y" antithesis and the punchy fragment for emphasis
  ("Users absorb that as normal. It isn't.").

## Two positive rules

- Plain words, active voice, one idea per sentence in the opening.
- Readable, not dry: lead with a concrete example and keep the prose flowing.

## Mechanics

- Active voice: "The team missed the deadline," not "was missed by the team."
  Passive only when the actor is unknown or irrelevant.
- Present tense for what a thing does: "This setting hides the sidebar."
- Address the reader as "you." "We" only for shared work you're part of.
- Condition before instruction: "If payment fails, retry once."
- One idea per sentence: split on a second "and" or a load-bearing "which."
- Define a term on first use: long form, short form in parentheses, then short
  form.
- Cut reader-blaming softeners: "simply," "just," "easy," "obviously," "of
  course."
- Cut filler openers: "It's worth noting that," "Basically," "At the end of the
  day."
- Sentence case for headings.
- Unambiguous dates: "2026-08-20" or "August 20, 2026," never "08/09."
- Technical writing: code, commands, filenames, and literals in monospace; UI
  names in bold.

## Cutting length

Revision bloats through repetition: a reframing gets patched into every section,
and one claim ends up stated five ways. Reading straight through won't catch it;
counting will.
- List the distinct claims (assertions, not sections); find and count each. Give
  a repeated claim one home — where the argument is developed, not previewed. A
  summary restating a developed claim is fine; the same argument at full strength
  twice is not.
- Sweep for dangling references — ordinals, comparatives, coined shorthand whose
  antecedent was cut. Name what each points at; if you can't, it dangles.
- When cuts run out and it's still too long, don't promise a length you can't
  hit. Say early: "hitting that length means dropping an argument — here are the
  candidates; which do you want to lose?"

## Structure is a separate pass

These rules fix prose, not structure. A malformed header, a claim ordered before
its setup, a section that overpromises — each fails independently. State the
format's fixed requirements explicitly and run its check or template. Only a
check guarantees structure.

## Reusable prompt block

Prepend when prompting a model to draft prose:

```text
Write this in a plain, direct voice. Follow these rules strictly:
1. No undefined jargon. Define any acronym or insider term in a few plain words on first use, or don't use it. Never stack several undefined terms in one sentence.
2. No throat-clearing. Don't announce what you're about to do, don't narrate structure, don't editorialize your reasoning. State the thing.
3. No showing off. No rhetorical triads, aphorisms, italics for drama, cute headings, or lines that exist to sound clever. Cut any sentence doing rhetorical work rather than carrying information.
4. Plain words, active voice, one idea per sentence in the opening.
5. Still readable — not choppy or dry. Lead with a concrete example and keep the prose flowing.
```

## Self-check

- Any acronym or specialist term undefined on first use?
- Any sentence announcing what you're about to do instead of doing it?
- Any line there to sound clever rather than inform?
- Gentle to read, or a list of assertions?

If the project or publication has a style guide, it wins where they disagree.

## Provenance

Distilled from [evanphx/llm-voice](https://github.com/evanphx/llm-voice): a
15-model study of how voice directives change model-written prose. Complements
the `unslop` skill (pattern removal) — plain-writing targets structural voice
rules (jargon, preamble, performative prose). See also
`knowledge/tools/llm-voice.md`.
